purpose: Evaluate whether the S602 Monitoring Framework's scheduled periodic review cadences should be converted to event-driven reviews, given that S604's first monitoring review confirmed findings identical to S602/S603 with zero drift signals fired and a monotonically worsening economic case.

cadences.name: Rapid Pulse
cadences.rationale: S604 was a comprehensive 10-agent review conducted 1 session ago. Its findings (0/4 gates FAIL, 0/24 triggers met, economic gate WORSENED, 0 drift signals, activation freeze SECURE) are identical to S603's findings. A Rapid Pulse at S605 would confirm the same result with no new data — the certified pool has not changed in 1 session, no drift signal has fired, and the economic case only worsens monotonically. The 6 DRIFT signals (DRIFT_001 through DRIFT_006) operate continuously between sessions and would immediately escalate any gate change, unauthorized artifact, charter modification, or authority claim — they do not wait for a scheduled review. A 1-session cadence on a dormant lane whose conditions degrade monotonically provides zero incremental governance value.
cadences.replacement: Rely on DRIFT_001 through DRIFT_006 for continuous monitoring. No scheduled replacement needed — event-driven signals cover all Rapid Pulse checks (gate re-evaluation, drift verification, cross-lane boundary scan). The economic gate recalculation (check 4) is the only forward-looking check but its trajectory is established: monotonically worsening. Recalculating at any cadence <20 sessions produces no new information.

cadences.name: Deep Audit
cadences.rationale: S600-S604 already established the full evidence ledger: (a) S724's 5-agent feasibility assessment demonstrated startup cost (4 sessions) exceeds projected savings (3 sessions), net-negative. (b) The economic gate WORSENED between S603 and S604 (remaining workload 299→289, amortization surface -3.3%). (c) The trajectory is monotonically worsening — 800-series certification will continue shrinking the remaining workload, making the breakeven increasingly unreachable. (d) AV_1 through AV_5 were evaluated at S724 and re-validated by S604 Agent C — all 5 require HIGH confidence, none are approaching threshold. (e) GAP-3 has survived 3 missed deadlines with 0/6 acceptances — no structural change is on the horizon. A deep audit at S620 would produce the same conclusion (CONTINUE DORMANCY) with slightly different numbers (certified pool ~2,300+, remaining ~250). The trend is established and unidirectional. More data points on the same curve do not change the governance recommendation.
triggers: DRIFT_002 fires — any mandatory gate transitions from FAIL to PASS (triggers immediate governance audit, not deferred to Deep Audit calendar)
DRIFT_006 fires — 800-series certification completes (100% Certified across all packs); triggers AV_4 re-evaluation
Economic gate recalculation shows net benefit ≥ 0 (requires substantial growth in remaining workload — counterfactual to current trajectory)
cadences.rationale_for_conversion: The Deep Audit's 8 checks are all derivative of the activation trigger registry and economic model, both of which are monitored continuously by drift signals. Binding the deep audit to events (gate transition, certification completion, or economic threshold crossed) ensures the audit fires when conditions ACTUALLY change, not when the calendar says to check whether conditions have changed. This eliminates governance overhead without reducing monitoring coverage.

cadences.name: Annual Stewardship
cadences.rationale: The Annual Stewardship's 6 checks span charter relevance, activation condition appropriateness, GAP-3 resolution status, S725 amendment need, stewardship principle compliance, and charter version-bumping. Of these: (a) Activation condition appropriateness (check 2) is monitored continuously by DRIFT_002 — a gate flip triggers immediate review. (b) GAP-3 resolution (check 3) is tracked by DRIFT_005 — resolution triggers update, non-resolution does not benefit from annual reaffirmation. (c) Stewardship principle compliance (check 5) plateaued at 85/100 (S604 Agent G) — the two violated principles (P1/P2) are GAP-3-dependent and won't change until GAP-3 is resolved, which is event-driven by DRIFT_005. (d) Charter relevance (checks 1, 4, 6) are genuine governance-health questions but for a lane that was never activated and whose conditions only worsen, the charter is a dormant document — it doesn't drift without modification (DRIFT_003 would fire). A year is excessive for a lane with zero operational activity.
triggers: Charter amendment proposed — any session modifies S600 Charter (DRIFT_003 variant: authorized modification with REVISION_HISTORY entry)
GAP-3 resolved — triggers Stewardship Framework reconciliation and P1/P2 re-evaluation
S725 Ownership Matrix amendment proposed — any change to Lane 600 governance structure
Portfolio structural change — e.g., 800-series completes, 300-series architecture shifts, new lane introduced
Fallback: if none of the above trigger by 2027-07-26, execute a LIGHTWEIGHT stewardship check (≤1 agent, read-only charter relevance confirmation, no full 6-check deep review)
cadences.fallback: LIGHTWEIGHT annual check if no event triggers by 2027-07-26. Scope: confirm charter still physically intact (hash unchanged), confirm GAP-3 status, confirm no new ownership gaps. Output ≤10 lines in REVISION_HISTORY.md. NOT a full S604-class 10-agent review.

recommended_event_triggers: DRIFT_002 — any mandatory gate transitions from FAIL to PASS
Economic threshold — net benefit ≥ 0 (counterfactual under current trajectory)
Charter amendment — S600 Charter modified with REVISION_HISTORY entry
GAP-3 resolution — Governance Board accepts S725 Row 16 (DRIFT_005 fires)
S725 Ownership Matrix amended for Lane 600
Portfolio structural change — new lanes introduced, 800-series architecture shifts
DRIFT_001/003/004 — any CRITICAL drift signal fires (immediate escalation, not deferred)
event_driven_rationale: The S602 Monitoring Framework's 6 DRIFT signals already constitute an event-driven monitoring system. DRIFT_001-004 cover all active threats (unauthorized artifacts, gate transitions, charter tampering, authority claims) with CRITICAL/HIGH severity and immediate escalation. DRIFT_005 tracks governance hygiene improvement. DRIFT_006 tracks the one portfolio milestone that could affect 600 relevance. Together with AGENTS.md §13.5 runtime drift signals (runtime artifact integrity, file hashes, parse counts), the monitoring surface is fully covered without scheduled reviews. The scheduled cadences are documenting what the drift signals would catch autonomously. For a dormant lane whose economic case monotonically worsens, calendar-driven confirmation of 'still dormant' provides zero marginal governance value.
drift_signals_rationale: Yes. The 6 DRIFT signals from S602, combined with AGENTS.md §13.5 runtime drift signals, form a complete monitoring surface: (1) DRIFT_001/003/004 (CRITICAL) — catch unauthorized artifacts, charter tampering, and authority claims with HALT-level severity. These are the highest-risk scenarios for a dormant lane and are caught immediately, not at the next scheduled review. (2) DRIFT_002 (HIGH) — catches the one event that could change the dormancy posture (gate transition). (3) DRIFT_006 (MEDIUM) — catches the portfolio milestone that triggers AV_4 re-evaluation. (4) AGENTS.md §13.5 — monitors runtime artifact integrity independently. The AGENTS.md signals cover the 'active runtime' dimension while the S602 DRIFT signals cover the 'dormant governance' dimension. No monitoring gap exists between the two layers.
activation_freeze_rationale: The activation freeze is structurally enforced by three independent mechanisms, none of which depend on periodic reviews: (1) S600 Charter §5.2 — requires Executive Board vote (all 3 leads) to activate. This is a procedural gate, not a monitoring gate. (2) S602 Activation Trigger Registry — 24 trigger conditions must be satisfied before activation review can be initiated. 0/24 are met and the trajectory is worsening. (3) Governance guard — BLOCK-level rules prevent unauthorized content modification. The 7 prohibited activation paths (S601 Board decision) remain intact. DRIFT_001/003/004 provide continuous enforcement with HALT escalation — they fire the moment unauthorized activity occurs, not when someone checks the calendar. Periodic reviews DOCUMENT that the freeze is secure; they do not ENFORCE it. Removing the documentation layer does not weaken the enforcement layer.
verdict_detail: The S602 Monitoring Framework's scheduled cadences (Rapid Pulse, Deep Audit, Annual Stewardship) should be converted to event-driven reviews keyed to the 6 DRIFT signals. T0 per-session checks remain as standard startup protocol (already covered by AGENTS.md §9). This reduces governance overhead from ~3 scheduled review sessions per year to zero scheduled sessions, with reviews firing only when drift signals indicate actual change. The monitoring surface remains complete — drift signals operate continuously, not at cadence boundaries. Economic recalculations at regular intervals on a monotonically worsening curve produce no new governance value. The Annual Stewardship's charter-health checks are converted to event-driven with a lightweight fallback if no trigger fires by 2027-07-26.

comparative_analysis.s604_vs_s605_delta: S604 was 1 session ago. Metrics between S603 and S604 changed by: certified pool +30 (2,181→2,211), remaining -10 (299→289). Between S604 and S605 the delta would be approximately +0 certified (no 800-series session in 1-session gap), +0 remaining. The Rapid Pulse would produce an identical result to S604 with the same 0/4 gates FAIL, 0/24 triggers met verdict. Zero informational value.
comparative_analysis.economic_trajectory: Monotonically worsening. Each 800-series certification session shrinks the remaining workload, reducing the amortization surface for the 600-series startup cost. The breakeven was already unreachable at 36 sessions vs. ~20-session horizon (S604 Agent E). Further shrinkage makes it LESS reachable, not more. No economic recalculation at any cadence changes the sign of the net benefit.
comparative_analysis.s604_confirmatory_not_investigative: S604 was designed to operationalize the S602 Monitoring Framework — to execute the first review and establish a baseline. It succeeded: the framework is operational, drift signals are clean, the activation freeze is secure. S604 was confirmatory by design. Subsequent reviews at the same depth (Rapid Pulse, Deep Audit) would be confirmatory by redundancy — confirming the same findings without the informational value of establishing a baseline.
comparative_analysis.drift_signal_coverage_completeness: DRIFT_001-006 cover: unauthorized artifacts (001), gate transitions (002), charter tampering (003), unauthorized authority claims (004), governance hygiene improvement (005), portfolio milestone triggers (006). Cross-referenced against the S604 Agent B gate audit (4 gates), Agent C trigger review (24 triggers), Agent D ownership monitoring (5 conflicts), Agent E economic reassessment (5 metrics), and Agent G stewardship review (5 principles): every dimension monitored by S604's 10 agents is covered by at least one drift signal. No dimension is monitored ONLY by scheduled review.

risk_of_cancellation.worst_case: A governance drift that none of the 6 DRIFT signals catch goes undetected for an extended period. The most plausible scenario: gradual erosion of charter assumptions (e.g., a governance standard change in the 800-series makes the S600 Charter's assumptions about certification workflow partially obsolete) without any single event dramatic enough to trigger a DRIFT signal. Severity: LOW. Even if the charter becomes partially obsolete, the lane is dormant — no operational decisions depend on charter accuracy. The charter would be refreshed before any activation (S600 Charter §9.1 requires Executive Board vote, which triggers charter review).
risk_of_cancellation.mitigation: The lightweight annual fallback (1-agent charter relevance check) catches slow charter drift. The AGENTS.md §13.5 runtime signals provide a second independent monitoring layer. Together these close the gap between 'event-driven signals for acute threats' and 'periodic check for gradual assumption drift.'
risk_of_cancellation.residual_risk: ACCEPTABLE. The residual risk of a dormant lane's charter becoming slightly misaligned with governance practice is orders of magnitude below the cost of 10-agent governance review sessions producing identical 'all clear' findings on a monotonically worsening curve.
